props.title: Farmageddon

sections.content: **Farmageddon (2011)** (2011) represents a pivotal moment in food industry documentaries, following the investigative path blazed by **Food, Inc.** (2008). Director Kristin Canty crafts a searing exposé of government raids on small family farms, revealing the stark power dynamics between agricultural regulators and local food producers. The film's raw footage of armed agents storming small dairy operations hits harder than polished corporate documentaries, drawing clear parallels to earlier whistleblowing docs like **The Future of Food** (2004).

sections.content: The wave of food system documentaries in the late 2000s marked a crucial shift in public awareness. **Food Fight** (2008) chronicled California's local food revolution, while Fresh (2009) highlighted innovative farmers creating sustainable alternatives. These films share Farmageddon's grassroots energy but take less confrontational approaches to advocating change.

Canty's personal stake as a mother seeking raw milk for her allergic son gives Farmageddon emotional weight missing from more academic food docs. This personal narrative approach influenced later films like Fed Up (2014) and **What the Health** (2017), though these focused more on nutrition and corporate influence than government overreach. sections.content: Farmageddon helped spark a new wave of regulatory-focused food documentaries. **More Than Honey** (2012) examined bee colony collapse and pesticide regulations, while **Seeds of Death** (2012) investigated GMO oversight. These films share Farmageddon's skepticism of government agencies but expand beyond dairy to broader agricultural policy issues.
